What does copyright infringement do to someone who infringes on another person’s copyright, or copyright holder’s proprietary rights?
Copyright infringement can take many forms and can actually be quite broad, depending on the context in which it occurs, however it generally occurs when it involves distributing content that someone else has created and copyrighted in one of several ways:

Reproduction - where the content in question is actually a copy of an existing work. If only a portion of an entire copyrighted piece is altered to form an unpublished work then the altered portion and the whole copyrighted piece still constitute the work in question, therefore would have to both be distributed and the copyright holder’s copyrighted rights must have been violated in either the original copyrighted piece or altered portion. For example if an author only wrote a portion of a novel but then distributed the entire novel under the author’s name without permission then that would be copyright infringement - unless the novel was actually published under the author’s name and published under that name by a publisher.

Distribution - where the content is actually being sold for profit and thus someone else is taking economic benefit from distributing the content that someone else has created. For example if an author sold copies of their novel under their own name without permission and someone else published and sold copies of the same novel under that publisher’s name and sold more copies than the author did then the author would have been infringing by selling the work when someone else was profiting from making money off it.

Distribution by misrepresentation - where the content is actually being sold at a price lower than that which the content creator actually intended and someone else was taking economic advantage from making the profit from the lower price. For example if an artist was selling their copyrighted artwork and someone else sold the same artwork at a price they weren’t authorized to sell the art at (the price was actually below the value or cost of the art because someone was profiting financially from others selling the same item to others).

A verb's tense can be changed by adding *-ed* or *-s*. These have different grammatical meanings, because tense describes how time has passed: Is the action happening at an earlier time or in the distant future, or both at once, or more recently, more immediately. The time in which an action or event happens changes our perception of the action.

Aspect describes how the action and its immediate surroundings are related: Is the action "done"/is "being done" right now, or is the thing the action is related to experiencing right now. The thing doing the action, called the "agent" here, is related to the action somehow or "by virtue of something".

Verb form isn’t made up out of mystery ingredients that you “click” into when you study English for a while and you have to learn which terms describe a verb’s tense and which term describes what aspect is related.
